title: Is a used lathe worth $2,500? Photos show wear, seller not answering
summary: A skeptical walk through a $2,500 used lathe listing when photos show wear and the seller goes quiet.

blocks.title: $2,500 asks a question the photos must answer
blocks.body: A classified listing shows a used bench/gap lathe for $2,500. The photos show ways wear and a bruised tailstock. The seller stopped answering messages. This page is how to decide without romanticizing "project iron."

blocks.heading: What the listing actually shows (example)
rows: Not a steal until spindle and ways are proven — price is a claim
Photos: shine on ways near the chuck
Could be wear polish; could be oil. Need a straightedge and light.
No thread-dial / incomplete change gears in photos
Seller silent after asking for spindle-play video
Treat silence as data — not as "they're busy, it's fine"
blocks.caption: Example listing details for grading. Not a real seller.

items.label: Spindle bearing play cold and warm
items.detail: Video with indicator preferred. Hand-feel alone is how people buy noise.

items.label: Way wear with a straightedge / photos under raking light
items.detail: Ask for it. If refused, walk.

items.label: Motor wiring voltage and phase
items.detail: A "deal" that needs a $900 RPC or VFD changes the math.

items.label: What tooling is included — named, not vibes
items.detail: Chuck condition, steady rest, change gears, wrenches.

items.label: Title / who can accept payment
items.detail: Scam pattern: urgency + silence + odd payment channel.

columns.name: If inspection passes
columns.detail: Example: $2,500 + transport + tooling gaps might still beat a worn $4k machine with paperwork — only with measurements.

columns.name: If seller stays silent
columns.detail: Your offer expires. Do not "hold space" for a ghost. Market listings exist elsewhere.

columns.name: If ways are hollowed
columns.detail: Scrap or parts value. Refeed / regrind economics often exceed the asking price on small lathes.

blocks.title: Red flags already present
blocks.body: Visible wear plus unanswered technical questions is enough to pause. A good seller of a good machine usually likes talking about the machine.

blocks.heading: Decision tree for this week
items: Send one clear message: ask for spindle-play video, way close-ups, voltage, and a reply deadline (48 hours).
If silence continues past the deadline — walk. Mark the listing mentally as unavailable.
If they answer with evidence, schedule an in-person check with indicator and straightedge — or pay a local tech for an hour.
Only then negotiate. Price drops are for known problems, not for mysteries.

blocks.heading: Skeptical check
blocks.prompt: The seller says "it's a solid machine, just busy, take it or leave it" and still sends no spindle video. Best move?
options: Wire the money today before someone else gets it
Treat missing evidence as a reason not to buy at $2,500
Assume ways wear is only cosmetic shine
blocks.explanation: Without measurements, $2,500 is a hope purchase. Silence after a specific ask is informative.
blocks.wrongFeedback: Re-read the red flags. Urgency without data is not a discount.

blocks.heading: Another lathe will appear
blocks.body: The scarce resource is a verifiable spindle and ways — not this particular listing.
